while a linked card or page stands docked, the docked panel is its reader
the body renders unconditionally inside the faded panel (the Sliver's shape), so the close fades the content instead of unmounting it and fading an empty box
no standing header (the tab row names it); the dock toggle is icon-only, its full wording on aria-label and title
the standing draw is the log's last turn, in this same window; there is one, never two; data-drawn is what the harness reads
"Try again" replays the exact request that failed (lastSendArgsRef)
the Free Write roster mounts in the shared chip row above the composer; absent outright in Draft, on screenplay and on a board
never `disabled`: a spent ask must answer a fourth press with a note; data-spent carries the quiet styling
the Draft roster takes the same slot in its own mode; chips render with the panel, never animate in, never reshuffle; the two rosters never co-render
what travels when you ask: behind a "?" beside the Ask box, no standing text
the note sits behind a "?" beside the lens heading
the nudges sleep: their section does not render and the engine (tutorNudges.ts) has no caller; the engine and its data stay, dormant
the Bible sits last in the cluster, only when the page rides a project; writer-authored, and nothing here can place text on a page

the type control: the fewest controls that do the act, the name in the aria-label; every form is a face button and - [ number ] +, the number typeable; choosing is the preview; - + are inert at the ends, never removed; mousedown preventDefault keeps the caret
a roster face, or `undefined` for Default: the host clears its stored face (no stored face = the theme's default)
where words can be highlighted (Draft, a card) the Typeface section carries the two scopes over the roster as a list; absent (Free Write, Revise): the face button
the highlight's size and the road that sizes only the highlighted words (one undo step), so - [N] + follow the scope as the face list does
the theme's own default first (a table checked against the CSS tokens), so "Default (<face>)" always names the face; the DOM read is the fallback
in the scoped form the face list is collapsed until the face button is pressed; it stays mounted (hidden), so it is the same list either way
the face in brass: an unchosen surface marks the "Default (<face>)" row, never a roster row (the theme picked it, not the writer)
the writer's installed fonts (device-local) follow the roster in both lists; a face not installed here shows a quiet note and renders as the default; "Add a font..." only in the scoped form
under Selection the size is the highlight's and a step sizes only the highlighted words; under Whole document it is the surface's
a surface is unborn while opened but empty: live and typeable, with no row; editors read it through useUnborn(id), which returns null once born

the unlock ceremony, the one accepted visible locked door; orange fires only the instant a territory is chosen; focus moves in and Tab is contained, so aria-modal is true; no Escape - the rite resolves in a choice

the caret lands in the card, so left/right step only while it is empty; PageUp/PageDown and the chevrons always step; the listener is registered once and reads the latest handler through a ref, so it never falls behind others
shared incentive pieces for ModeStage and JournalEntry; the word goal is a lap: crossing it fills the bar orange with a pulse, then it resets
laps are seeded from the first render, so a page opened with words already written never celebrates an earlier session's laps

milestone celebrations: seeded per plan (scopeKey) from the FULL lit set on the first render after boot, so only beats lit this app-load celebrate; seenLit commits when the pulse completes, so an interrupted one is shown again
the circle-bar projects beat coverage, glanceable only; pointer-events:none is an invariant (no exit door on a writing surface); rightSlot keeps the timer beside it
the theme's own Wrizo mark: Arbor's hand-drawn PNG, Flux's own WRIZO wordmark in the chrome face - never Arbor's picture
Catch: one shared capture gesture behind three doors; it creates no row - it opens an unborn surface, and the page is born by the first word

a dissolved surface is pointer-events:none and cannot be hovered, so the engine tests the pointer against every dissolving surface's rect; an element with data-open="false" is closed whatever its opacity
turning Fade off mid-dissolve resurfaces the chrome at once, not at the next trigger
keyboard focus outside the text restores the chrome, as a pointer reaching it does

the shared typewriter engine holds the active line low so earlier lines ride up and fade; past the zone's lower bound it scrolls smoothly by exactly the delta (one line for ordinary typing), never a jolt
the start offset is a visual quarter of the stage, for prose, script and the Journal alike
the row the collapsed caret sits in, or null: a fresh line after Enter is an empty row, where the range gives no rect or the previous line's
diagnostics in memory only: an array the harness puts on window before mount; absent in every real session, so nothing is written
the fade trigger: window mode gates on the sheet's own top vs the viewport, container mode on the box's own scrollTop against its rest position
one line per glide: the next step waits until the last glide has landed and steps from there; a glide that never lands stops waiting after GLIDE_MS
a glide is paid only when it lands: one that ends short (the browser cancelled it) has its remainder owed again; one that went back past its start is the writer's own scroll, honoured
glides are timed by performance.now(), ending at LINE_GLIDE_MS whatever the frame pacing; a backlog is paid in bigger steps finished within BACKLOG_CAP_MS
no single catch-up step is more than MAX_STEP_LINES lines, however much is owed: a deep backlog takes more steps, never a bigger one
the band mask's line unit in screen px (line height x paint scale); zoomed, the start offset puts a fresh page's first line at the anchor
room below the last line, so it can rise to the anchor: the column's own height in layout px
the caret's ROW is the truth when the range's rect is not on it, so Enter's line is paid at once
the caret is tracked in document space (from the TEXT's top, not the scroller's padding), so a writer's own scroll is never snapped back and a scale change never shifts it
the restore re-asserts at rAF + 80/200/350ms to win the mount race, and cancels the later ones the moment the writer acts
